Simulate BOIN-ETC Trials

Source: R/boin_etc_simulate.R
boin_etc_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of the BOIN-ETC design of Kakizume et al. (2024), which finds the optimal dose combination of two drugs given together by dividing the dose matrix into subtrials along which the DLT probability increases (the waterfall approach) and running the BOIN-ET design of Takeda et al. (2018) within each subtrial. Return the patients, DLTs and responses at every combination. This is the simulation engine behind sim_boin_etc.

Usage

boin_etc_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  subtrials = c("etc1", "etc2", "etc3"),
  n_earlystop = 6,
  etc1_start = c("diagonal", "below"),
  rule4 = c("paper", "authors_code"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  p_eli = NULL,
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, phi.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, delta, as in sim_boin_et.

p_true

Numeric matrix. True DLT probability of every combination, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B. At least two levels of each drug.

p_resp

Numeric matrix of the same size. True response probability of every combination.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial; with cohort_size it gives the maximum sample size.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

subtrials

Character scalar. The division of the dose matrix into subtrials and their starting combinations: "etc1" (the default), "etc2" or "etc3", BOIN-ETC1, 2 and 3 of the figures and tables of Kakizume et al. (2024). See Details.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. A subtrial ends when the combination chosen for the next cohort has this many patients (n_stop of Kakizume et al., 2024). Defaults to 6.

etc1_start

Character scalar. Starting combination of a row subtrial of "etc1": "diagonal" (the default) one level of drug B below the candidate of the previous subtrial, as the text and the figures of Kakizume et al. (2024) state; "below" the same level of drug B, the rule of the code of the authors that produced their published results. See Details.

rule4

Character scalar. Choice among the neighboring combinations when the DLT rate is between lambda1 and lambda2 and the response rate at most eta1: "paper" (the default) the rule of the text; "authors_code" the rule of the code of the authors, needed to reproduce their results for BOIN-ETC1. See Details.

p_saf, p_tox, p_saf_resp, prior

Design parameters of the BOIN-ET boundaries, as in boin_et_boundary. The defaults give (lambda1, lambda2, eta1) = (0.14, 0.35, 0.48) for a target DLT probability of 0.30 and a target response probability of 0.60.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A combination is excluded, with the higher combinations of its subtrial, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds p_eli is above this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the exclusion rule. Defaults to NULL, target.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type. Defaults to 0, as in the simulations of Kakizume et al. (2024); the BOIN-ET functions default to 0.2.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) or "binary", as in sim_boin_et.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_etc_trials, which is a list with components

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp, n_tox_resp

Integer arrays with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B, of the patients treated, the DLTs, the responses and the patients with both a DLT and a response.

excluded

Logical array of the same dimensions, TRUE for the combinations excluded by the DLT rule during the trial.

cohorts_used, n_subtrials

Integer vectors of the cohorts enrolled and of the subtrials run.

stop_reason

Character vector: "lowest_excluded" (the lowest combination was excluded), "subtrials_completed" or "max_cohorts" (the maximum sample size was reached).

early_stop

Logical vector, TRUE for the trials stopped because the lowest combination was excluded. These trials select no optimal dose combination.

design

"BOIN-ETC1", "BOIN-ETC2" or "BOIN-ETC3".

boundary

List with lambda1, lambda2 and eta1.

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

With L levels of drug A and M of drug B (AaBb is the combination of level a of drug A and level b of drug B), the first subtrial is A1B1, A2B1, ..., ALB1, ALB2, ..., ALBM, started at A1B1. Then:

"etc1", "etc2"

one subtrial per row l = L - 1, ..., 1, AlB2, ..., AlBM. When the candidate of the first subtrial is AlB1, the rows start at row l - 1 (at row 1 when l is 1) and the rows above are skipped. "etc2" starts every row at its lowest combination. "etc1" starts the row below the candidate AlBm of the previous subtrial at level m - 1 of drug B (etc1_start = "diagonal") or at level m ("below"), and at level 2 when that level is 1, after a candidate in the first column and after a subtrial that ended without one.

"etc3"

L-shaped subtrials j = 1, ..., min(L, M) - 1: column j + 1 of drug B from level 1 of drug A up to level L - j, then row L - j from column j + 2 to M, each started at its lowest combination. With L > M the shapes run out of columns after M - 1 of them, which still covers the matrix.

Within a subtrial, after each cohort at a combination with DLT rate p and response rate q: the combination and the higher combinations of the subtrial are excluded when its DLT data fail the rule of cutoff_eli; the subtrial ends without a candidate when its lowest combination is excluded, and the trial ends when that combination is A1B1. Otherwise the next cohort escalates when p <= lambda1 and q <= eta1 (it stays at the highest combination of the subtrial and below an excluded one), de-escalates when p >= lambda2 (it stays at the lowest), stays when q > eta1, and otherwise (rule 4) goes to the next combination up if it has not been treated, or else to the treated, not excluded combination of the current one and its two neighbors in the subtrial with the highest response rate, a tie being broken at random. The subtrial ends when the combination chosen for the next cohort has n_earlystop patients (that combination is the candidate of the subtrial), and the trial ends when all cohorts have been enrolled or all subtrials have been run.

Kakizume et al. (2024) do not state the rules in every case; the following were checked against their code and their published results (inst/reproduce/reproduce_Kakizume2024.R):

  • The text of Section 2.2 describes BOIN-ETC2 with the L-shaped subtrials and BOIN-ETC3 with the rows started at their lowest combination. Their Figure 2 and Supplementary Figures S1 and S2, their tables and their code have it the other way round, and so has this function.

  • The text and the figures start a row of BOIN-ETC1 one level of drug B below the previous candidate ("diagonal"); the code that produced the tables starts it at the same level ("below"), and only that rule reproduces the published allocation.

  • In rule 4, the code of the authors drops the response rate of an untreated combination below the current one but not the combination, so that the choice moves one combination down (from the current combination to the untreated one, or from the one above to the current one); it also breaks a tie among the first eligible combinations rather than among the tied ones. rule4 = "authors_code" applies these rules. An untreated combination below the current one only happens in BOIN-ETC1, and its published allocation is reproduced only with these rules.

  • The code excludes only the current combination and may treat an excluded lowest combination again; here the text is followed (the published results do not depend on the difference). The text does not say what happens when A1B1 is excluded.

The response of a patient does not exclude a combination, as in Kakizume et al. (2024). Each patient draws two uniform variates in enrollment order, the first for the DLT and the second for the response; a tie under rule 4 draws one more after the cohort.

References

Kakizume, T., Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2024). BOIN-ETC: A Bayesian optimal interval design considering efficacy and toxicity to identify the optimal dose combinations. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 33(4), 716-727. doi:10.1177/09622802241236936

Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2018). BOIN-ET: Bayesian optimal interval design for dose finding based on both efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(4), 383-395. doi:10.1002/pst.1864

See also

sim_boin_etc, boin_etc_select_obd, boin_et_simulate

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Kakizume et al. (2024)
p_true <- matrix(c(0.05, 0.10, 0.10, 0.30, 0.30, 0.50), nrow = 2)
p_resp <- matrix(c(0.10, 0.25, 0.25, 0.60, 0.60, 0.65), nrow = 2)
trials <- boin_etc_simulate(
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60, p_true = p_true, p_resp = p_resp,
  n_cohort = 8, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated BOIN-ETC1 trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   dose levels          : 2 of drug A, 3 of drug B
#>   target DLT rate      : 0.3
#>   target response rate : 0.6
#>   cohorts              : 8 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 24
#>   subtrial end (n_stop): 6
#> 
#> Patients treated, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 3.22 4.16 4.36
#> A2 4.22 5.24 1.32
#> 
#> DLTs observed, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 0.18 0.38 1.33
#> A2 0.44 1.52 0.69
#> 
#> Responses observed, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 0.27 1.01 2.70
#> A2 1.00 3.21 0.81
#> 
#> Average number of subtrials: 2
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#>         max_cohorts subtrials_completed 
#>                  61                  39
